evidence_quotes.quote: In conclusion, B. licheniformis DSM 13 produces an antimicrobial substance that represents the two-peptide lantibiotic lichenicidin and that shows activity against a wide range of Gram-positive bacteria including methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains.

Here we report the identification and antibacterial activity of the new two-peptide lantibiotic lichenicidin and the antibacterial spectrum of an unanticipated substance that is present in the culture supernatant.

In order to demonstrate the connection between the lantibiotic gene cluster and one of the antibacterial activities, two Bacillus licheniformis DSM 13 mutant strains harbouring insertions in the structural genes of the modification enzymes licM1 and licM2 were constructed.

In conclusion, this study shows that B. licheniformis DSM 13 produces a novel two-peptide lantibiotic that is associated with the cell surface and that shows stability against trypsin, chymotrypsin and the proteases of the culture supernatant of the producer.

criterion_notes.c1: Does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access; this is a microbiology and biochemistry laboratory study of peptide antibiotic (lantibiotic) production by Bacillus licheniformis DSM 13.
criterion_notes.c2: Fails both the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Under the plain wording, the study examines no legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor (references to 'regulation' in the paper refer solely to bacterial genetic regulation such as lanR/lanK). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, there is no rule-type mechanism governing service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff or cost-recovery rules, discretion or accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical laboratory data generated through bioinformatic sequence analysis, plasmid-insertion mutagenesis, RP-HPLC fractionation, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, stability assays, and agar well diffusion antimicrobial assays.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports biochemical and microbiological outcomes (bacterial growth inhibition zones, minimum inhibitory concentrations against Gram-positive indicator strains including MRSA, peptide molecular masses, and protease/heat/pH stability) rather than any water or sanitation access, connection, availability, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion outcome.
criterion_notes.c5: Within its microbiology domain, the experimental design, bacterial strains (unit of analysis: bacterial cultures/isolates), genetic and biochemical manipulations, and antimicrobial activity outcomes are clearly reported; however, all are unrelated to water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in English.

study_design: Laboratory experimental microbiology and molecular genetics study
population_and_sample: Bacterial strains in vitro: producer strain Bacillus licheniformis DSM 13 (and transformable variant MW3 plus insertion mutants LicM1INT and LicM2INT) tested against a panel of Gram-positive and Gram-negative indicator strains including clinical MRSA isolates
exposure: Plasmid-insertion inactivation of lantibiotic modification enzyme genes (licM1 and licM2) and exposure of indicator bacteria to B. licheniformis culture supernatant and isopropanol cell wash extracts
outcome: Peptide molecular masses (MALDI-TOF), protease/thermal/pH stability, bacterial growth inhibition zones, and minimum inhibitory concentrations against Gram-positive bacteria including MRSA
rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic). Full text matches the metadata and reports an experimental microbiology and biochemistry study characterizing the biosynthesis, structure, stability, and antibacterial efficacy of the two-peptide lantibiotic lichenicidin from Bacillus licheniformis DSM 13. It does not examine water or sanitation service access (c1=no), any legal/administrative/governance factor under either the plain or narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading (c2=no), or any water/sanitation access outcome (c4=no).
